title: Measuring Globalisation: KOF and AT Kearney
welcome_lead: How do you measure the deepening of global connections? Explore the KOF index and rivals.
meta_desc: Geography HL Adventure: KOF Globalisation Index, AT Kearney and measurement of globalisation.
final_note: You have weighed how to measure global connection. The metrics frame how we see the process.

concepts.def: Process of intensifying economic, social, political and cultural integration across borders.

walkthroughs.body_html: The KOF Index measures economic (trade, FDI), social (information flows, personal contacts, cultural proximity) and political (international cooperation) dimensions, distinguishing de facto from de jure measures. Top-ranked countries are typically small, open economies like Switzerland, Netherlands and Belgium.

The AT Kearney/Foreign Policy index, published 2001-2007, ranked countries on economic integration, personal contact, technological connectivity and political engagement. Singapore and Ireland often topped rankings; it was criticised for skewing toward small states.

David Harvey's 'time-space compression' captures how cheaper transport, instant communication and digital platforms erode distance as a constraint. The COVID-19 pandemic revealed both the resilience and fragility of these connections.
